reviews.quote: HP's EliteBook Ultra G1i combines the efficiency of Lunar Lake with a premium business chassis — long battery life and an excellent 2.8K display.

praises: 2.8K 120Hz touch panel is sharper than most business ultrabooks and great for text
Lunar Lake 258V + 32GB: quiet, cool, all-day battery for road-warrior work
Arc 140V handles light video edits and casual gaming far better than old Iris Xe
Business-grade security stack (Wolf, vPro manageability, fingerprint + IR cam shutter)
Sub-1.4 kg with a real port selection including HDMI and USB-A
complaints: Pricing at/near $3,000 CAD is MacBook Pro territory for an iGPU machine
Marketplace stock at Best Buy; direct HP CA configurator is confusing on this model
Soldered everything — 512GB base on a $2,800 machine
Fan curve can pulse audibly on fast chargers while lid closed (docking scenario)
HP Wolf trial software nags on consumer-style first boot

design_philosophy: HP's business flagship clamshell: the EliteBook Ultra replaces the old Dragonfly role — thin light-and-light aluminium, security-first firmware, and Lunar Lake efficiency for executives. The 258V/32GB tier is the sweet spot of the range.
rating_notes: Inferred from Lunar Lake business-ultrabook anchors (same 258V/32GB/Arc 140V as ThinkPad X1C G13 class in dataset): battery 9.0, Arc 140V gaming 3.5 per calibration.
